name: Question 2
problem:
Consider the first-order linear ODE

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-3y=5.
$$

We wish to solve this equation using the method of variation of parameters (VOP).

Select the correct options below.

$\,$ According to VOP, we assume a particular solution of the form {{field-1}}.

$\,$ Solving for $u,$ we have $u(x)=$ {{field-2}}.

$\,$ Therefore, the particular solution is ${y}_{p}(x)=$ {{field-3}}.
worked_solution:
To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

To find the complementary solution ${y}_{c},$ we solve the corresponding homogeneous equation, given by

$$
{y}_{c}^{′}-3{y}_{c}=0.
$$

Solving this equation, we find that the complementary solution is

$$
{y}_{c}=A{e}^{3x}
$$

where $A$ is an arbitrary constant.

The method of variation of parameters constructs a particular solution by varying the constant in the homogeneous solution. So, to find a suitable ${y}_{p},$ we set $A=u(x)$ in the complementary solution, as given by the following ansatz:

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=u(x){e}^{3x}
$$

Intuitively, this form of ${y}_{p}$ tracks the homogeneous solution but with a varying amplitude.

To find $u,$ we substitute our ansatz into the equation, apply the product rule to the derivative term, and simplify to isolate ${u}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{(u{e}^{3x})}^{′}-3(u{e}^{3x}) & =5 \\ {u}^{′}{e}^{3x}+3u{e}^{3x}-3u{e}^{3x} & =5 \\ {u}^{′}{e}^{3x}+\cancel{3u{e}^{3x}}-\cancel{3u{e}^{3x}} & =5 \\ {u}^{′}{e}^{3x} & =5 \\ {u}^{′} & =5{e}^{-3x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$ (omitting the arbitrary constant), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{′} & =5{e}^{-3x} \\ \int {u}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =\int 5{e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x \\ u & =-\frac{5}{3}{e}^{-3x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since ${y}_{p}=u(x){e}^{3x},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p} & =u(x){e}^{3x} \\  & =-\frac{5}{3}{e}^{-3x}\cdot {e}^{3x} \\  & =-\frac{5}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the first-order linear ODE dydx−3y=5. We wish to solve this equation using the method of variation of parameters (VOP).

Select the correct options below.

According to VOP, we assume a particular solution of the form
u(x)e2x
u(x)e3x
u(x)e2x
u(x)e−3x
u(x)e5x
u(x)e−5x
.

Solving for u, we have u(x)=
−53e−3x
53e−3x
−53e5x
−53e−3x
−53e3x
−52e−2x
.

Therefore, the particular solution is yp(x)=
−53
−53e3x

EXPLANATION

To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

To find the complementary solution yc, we solve the corresponding homogeneous equation, given by yc′−3yc=0.

Solving this equation, we find that the complementary solution is yc=Ae3x where A is an arbitrary constant.

The method of variation of parameters constructs a particular solution by varying the constant in the homogeneous solution. So, to find a suitable yp, we set A=u(x) in the complementary solution, as given by the following ansatz:

yp(x)=u(x)e3x

Intuitively, this form of yp tracks the homogeneous solution but with a varying amplitude.

To find u, we substitute our ansatz into the equation, apply the product rule to the derivative term, and simplify to isolate u′:

(ue3x)′−3(ue3x)=5u′e3x+3ue3x−3ue3x=5u′e3x+3ue3x−3ue3x=5u′e3x=5u′=5e−3x

Integrating both sides with respect to x (omitting the arbitrary constant), we have u′=5e−3x∫u′dx=∫5e−3xdxu=−53e−3x.

Finally, since yp=u(x)e3x, we have

yp=u(x)e3x=−53e−3x⋅e3x=−53.
